content:
Grab rails are a simple adaptation that can make moving around the home safer.

This guide explains where rails help most and how to get them. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Where rails help

  • By the toilet.
  • In the bath or shower.
  • Beside steps at the front or back door.
  • On the stairs, as a second banister.

Choosing rails

  • Thicker or textured rails are easier to grip.
  • Rails must be fixed securely to a solid wall.
  • The position depends on how you move, so an assessment helps.

Getting them fitted

Ask your council for an OT assessment. In England, minor adaptations costing under £1,000 should be provided free if you are assessed as needing them. Rules differ in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. Larger adaptations may need a Disabled Facilities Grant.

Avoid unsafe supports

Towel rails, sinks and furniture are not designed to take your weight.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I fit rails myself?

You can, but they must be securely fixed. An OT can advise on position.

Are rails free?

Often, after a council assessment.
